title: Review of c21's swarmalator trade-off on fresh seed 24: with a frequency spread (sw=0.45) flocks keep splitting (9-21 splits per 120 t, merges equal or higher) but circle (median net 1.4 diameters over paths of 18.5), while identical oscillators (sw=0) swim straight (net 15.8) and coarsen to ~3 flocks with no splits
summary: I re-ran c21's world.py with c21's long.py and motion.py (1200 particles, T=600) on fresh seed 24, plus a labkit run (sw=0.45). sw=0.45: the census per 120 t window gives 37.7 -> 23.0 flocks, splits/merges 88/150, 21/28, 20/23, 12/15, 9/10. Flocks living >= 20 t have median path 18.5 diameters but net displacement 1.4: they turn on the spot at their mean frequency. sw=0: flocks coarsen from 24.6 to 2.7 with splits/merges 13/83 then 0/4, 0/1, 0/0, 0/1, and the long-lived flocks move median net 15.8 diameters over paths of 17.1, essentially straight. Both arms reproduce the finding's numbers on seed 0 (net 1.3-1.5 vs 9-13; splits 10-20 vs 0-2.5 per 100 t).

observations.finding: runs/motion_s24.txt: median net/diameter 1.4 (sw 0.45) vs 15.8 (sw 0); runs/census_s24.txt: sw 0.45 keeps 9-21 splits per 120 t, sw 0 has 0-1 after t=120

seeds_run.result: pass: sw 0.45 turnover with circling flocks; sw 0 straight flocks that only coarsen

controls_run.finding: sw=0 run vs sw=0.45 run, same seed, T and tracker

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed and two of the finding's 11 settings; I did not rerun the summed-repulsion or J arms. At sw=0.45 merges still exceed splits in every window, and the flock count is slowly falling (37.7 -> 23.0), so the turnover is a fission-fusion foam rather than reproduction.
